text_blocks.snippet: Citizens Bank in Sac City, Iowa, failed due to significant loan losses, particularly in commercial trucking loans, stemming from lax lending practices and inadequate risk management. The bank's Board and management failed to properly oversee lending to the commercial trucking industry, leading to a concentration of risky loans. When the trucking industry faced financial difficulties, Citizens Bank compounded the problem by extending more credit through overdrafts, further eroding the bank's capital and liquidity.

list.title: Lax Lending Practices:
list.snippet: Citizens Bank made loans to commercial trucking companies without sufficient risk assessment, expertise, or Board oversight.

list.title: Concentration Risk:
list.snippet: A significant portion of the bank's portfolio was tied to commercial trucking loans, making it vulnerable to industry-specific downturns.

list.title: Compounding Problems:
list.snippet: When the trucking industry experienced financial strain, Citizens Bank continued lending through overdrafts, worsening the situation.

list.title: Erosion of Capital and Liquidity:
list.snippet: The combination of loan losses and continued lending depleted the bank's capital and strained its ability to meet its obligations.

list.title: Inadequate Risk Management:
list.snippet: The FDIC OIG report highlighted the bank's failure to implement recommended corrective actions to improve its financial safety and soundness.

list.title: State and FDIC Intervention:
list.snippet: The Iowa Division of Banking closed the bank and appointed the FDIC as receiver.
